She revisited it in 2010, adding segments on HIV testing, the Iraq War and crack cocaine. But essentially it’s still a piece for five actors, two of them doubling parts, each character nameless except for referencing a colour – “Lady in Yellow” etc, representing the seven shades in the rainbow.

Page’s production has an excellent cast, who deliver the necessary intensity and occasional hilarity, and perform choreographer Ingrid Mackinnon’s moves with evident pleasure as well as concentration.

cn.t: Shange's 50-year-old choreopoem finally reaches London in a well-received production that delivers Black female experiences with feeling, though some critics note the staging rushes through its poetic scenes.
